common_name: Onyx Odyssey Hellebore (Winter Jewels Series Near-Black Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Onyx Odyssey is part of the Winter Jewels breeding series and produces some of the darkest, near-black flowers available in hellebores, blooming in late winter to early spring.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, keeping soil evenly moist while the plant establishes. Onyx Odyssey is part of the acclaimed Winter Jewels hellebore breeding series and stands out for flowers in an unusually deep, glossy near-black purple, one of the darkest colors available among Lenten roses, held above leathery, evergreen, deeply divided foliage. Like other Lenten roses it blooms very early, often through late-season snow or hard frost, providing color in the shade garden when almost nothing else is flowering. Remove tattered old foliage in late winter just before bloom to showcase the flowers, and note that all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested, so site it away from areas where pets or children graze.
sources: Northwest Garden Nursery — Winter Jewels hellebore breeding

common_name: Josef Lemper Hellebore (Vigorous Pure White Christmas Rose)

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in partial to full shade; Josef Lemper is a vigorous, floriferous Christmas rose selection that blooms earlier and more heavily than the straight species, often flowering around the winter holidays in mild climates.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, slightly alkaline, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, keeping soil evenly moist through establishment. Josef Lemper is a superior selection of the traditional Christmas rose, valued for producing more flowers per plant and blooming earlier and more reliably than older seed-grown Helleborus niger, often opening its large, pure white, saucer-shaped flowers around the winter holiday season in mild climates and continuing into late winter elsewhere. The dark, leathery, evergreen foliage stays attractive year-round, providing structure in the shade garden even between bloom seasons. Remove old, tattered leaves in late winter just before flowering to best display the blooms, and keep in mind that all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Frohnleiten is a vigorous, evergreen epimedium selection that spreads into a good-sized groundcover patch faster than many slower epimedium species.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, where it tolerates dry shade under trees better than most shade perennials once established. Frohnleiten is a vigorous, evergreen to semi-evergreen epimedium hybrid producing sprays of bright yellow flowers with reddish-bronze centers in spring, held just above heart-shaped leaves that emerge coppery-bronze and mature to leathery green, often taking on burgundy tones again in winter. It spreads at a good pace into a dense, weed-suppressing groundcover, faster than many other epimedium species, making it useful for covering larger areas of dry shade under trees or shrubs. Cut back old foliage in late winter before new growth and flowers emerge to keep the planting looking fresh.

common_name: Sweet Tea Heucherella (Amber-Copper Ruffled Foliage Heucherella)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Sweet Tea holds its warm amber-copper foliage color well through the season and tolerates more heat than many heucherella cultivars.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade, with mulch to keep roots cool and moist. Sweet Tea is a popular heucherella cultivar prized for its large, deeply ruffled, maple-shaped leaves in a warm amber-to-copper color that deepens further in cooler weather, providing months of foliage interest well beyond its modest sprays of small white flowers in late spring. As a heucherella, it combines the bold, colorful foliage typical of heuchera with a more vigorous, ground-covering habit inherited from its foamflower parentage, spreading gradually to fill in a shaded bed. It pairs well with blue-green hostas, ferns, and dark-leafed heuchera, and benefits from being divided every few years in spring or fall as the clump matures.

common_name: Alabama Sunrise Heucherella (Bright Gold-to-Red Seasonal Color-Change Heucherella)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Alabama Sunrise changes color dramatically through the season, emerging bright gold in spring and deepening toward orange-red as temperatures cool in fall.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade, with mulch to keep roots cool. Alabama Sunrise is a heucherella cultivar grown chiefly for its dramatic seasonal color transformation, unfurling bright gold-yellow leaves with red veining in spring that gradually shift toward warm orange and finally deep red-bronze tones as the weather cools in fall, giving the planting a constantly changing look through the growing season. Like other heucherella it spreads gradually to form a groundcover-like patch, combining the colorful foliage of heuchera with the vigorous habit of foamflower, and produces modest sprays of small white flowers in late spring that are secondary to its foliage display. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring or fall to maintain vigor.
